newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Capricorn up on nickel assay results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Capricorn up on nickel assay results.

text.p: The shares of Capricorn Resources Australia NL rose sharply in early trade on Thursday after encouraging nickel assay results were announced from the Roundtop joint venture in Western Australia on Wednesday.
At 10.35 a.m. (2335 GMT), Capricorn shares were 4.5 cents firmer at 27 cents on turnover of 4.95 million shares.

The Roundtop joint venture consists of Capricorn Resources with 25 percent and the remainder held by the Lake Johnston joint venture group which is equally owned by Forrestania Gold Nl and South African-based Gencor Ltd.
"The stock is benefiting from the good results from Roundtop," a Perth-based dealer said.

Late on Wednesday, Forrestania said a second diamond drill hole at the Emily Ann prospect within the Roundtop joint venture site, located three km north of Maggie Hays, encountered two zones of massive sulphide mineralisation of 1.05 metres at depth of 213.3 metres and 3.3 metres at a depth of 234.1 metres.

Forrestania reported on February 21 that the first drill hole at Emily Ann intersected 10.7 metres at 2.39 percent nickel with a broader zone of 14.7 metres at 1.94 percent. A zone of 0.85 metres had 8.98 percent nickel.
Forrestania shares were steady at A$2.94. Forrestania is currently subject to a cash and scrip agreed takeover offer from Linore Mining International Ltd of Canada.
